root.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Karpov Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nd7

overview: Black recaptures dxe4 and plays ...Nd7 so that ...Ngf6 can trade off White's active knight without doubling pawns. White continues 5.Nf3 Ngf6 6.Nxf6+ or 6.Ng3 with ...e6 and ...Bd6 (Kasparov Attack). Black reaches a sound, compact set-up with ...Bf5 or ...e6 and few weaknesses.

white_ideas.idea: Nf3, Ng3 and Bd3 with the bishop pair-free space edge, aiming at kingside play
Nxf6+ and Bc4 or Qe2, keeping a small initiative

typical_structures.structure: Caro-Kann c6/e6 structure against d4, with the d-file half-open

character.notes: Classic solid Caro-Kann set-up; a few sharper sub-lines such as Ng3 attacks.

soundness.notes: Sound; one of the main Caro-Kann lines.

structure.notes: Half-open d-file but centre more fluid than the Exchange.

approach.notes: A standard choice, not a universal system.

level.notes: Plans are clear; some theory in the Kasparov Attack.

sublines_that_differ.name: Kasparov Attack 6.Ng3 e6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nd7 5. Nf3 Ngf6 6. Ng3
sublines_that_differ.how: Sharper kingside play with 7.Bd3 and Qe2.

character.reason: Caro-Kann with few weaknesses and steady play.

structure.reason: Caro-Kann with a half-open d-file; could read as flexible.

plans.reason: No plan on the list fits clearly.
